[[File:Barbara Wohlmuth.jpg|thumb|Wohlmuth at [[Oberwolfach]], 2014]]
'''Barbara I. Wohlmuth''' is a German [[mathematician]] specializing in the numerical solution of [[partial differential equation]]s. She holds the [[TUM Department of Mathematics|chair of numerical mathematics]] at the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM).{{r|ll}}

==Education and career==
Wohlmuth earned a master's degree in mathematics in 1991 from [[Joseph Fourier University]] in France, and a diploma in 1992 from TUM.{{r|ll}}
She completed a doctorate at TUM in 1995, under the supervision of Ronald Hoppe,{{r|ll|mgp}} and earned her [[habilitation]] in 2000 at the [[University of Augsburg]].

She worked as a full professor at the [[University of Stuttgart]] from 2001 until 2010, when she returned to TUM.{{r|ll}}

==Recognition==
In 2005, the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]] in Milan gave her their [[International Giovanni Sacchi Landriani Prize]]. She won the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] in 2012.{{r|gwlp}} In 2013 she was elected to the [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].{{r|ab3}} In 2020 she was named a [[SIAM Fellow]] "for sustained seminal contributions to the field of numerical mathematics and for exemplary leadership and service to the computational science community".{{r|sif}} She was elected to the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in 2022.{{r|leo}}

She was the [[Emmy Noether]] Lecturer of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2014,{{r|noether}} and an invited speaker on numerical analysis and scientific computing at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|icm}}
